title: Local fibre-Cartier criterion for a locally principal subscheme
statement: Let φ:X\to S be a flat morphism locally of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let Z be a closed subscheme of X, and let x\in Z with image s\in S. Assume that Z is locally principal in a neighbourhood of x, that is, there is an open neighbourhood of x on which the ideal sheaf of Z is locally generated by a single section, and that the fibre Z_s\subseteq X_s is an effective Cartier divisor [def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor] in a neighbourhood of x. Then there is an open neighbourhood U of x such that Z\cap U is a relative effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier] on U over S.

proof.text:
The assertion is local on X. Choose affine opens Spec(A)
i s of S and Spec(B)
i x of X with φ(Spec(B))\subseteq Spec(A); let p\subset A and q\subset B be the primes of s and x, and I\subseteq B the ideal of Z\cap Spec(B). Then A	o B is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Replacing B by a localization B_h with h
otin q (still flat and finitely presented over A, and Spec(B_h) is an open neighbourhood of x) we may assume, by the two hypotheses, that I=(f) is principal and that Z_s\cap Spec(B) is an effective Cartier divisor [def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor] in X_s\cap Spec(B)=Spec(B\otimes_Aκ(p)). The latter says that every prime P of B\otimes_Aκ(p) has an element g_P
otin P such that the extension of I to (B\otimes_Aκ(p))_{g_P} is generated by a nonzerodivisor (for P not containing the image of I take g_P in that image; the extended ideal is then the unit ideal). No flatness of B/I over A is assumed: it is part of the conclusion.

Apply [lem-pc-algebra-fibre-cartier-local] to A, B, K=κ(p), the principal ideal I and the prime q, whose contraction to A is p, the kernel of A\to κ(p). It gives g\in B, g\notin q, such that IB_g is generated by a nonzerodivisor of B_g and B_g/IB_g is flat over A. Put U=Spec(B_g), an open neighbourhood of x. Then Z\cap U=V(IB_g) is an effective Cartier divisor in U, and Z\cap U\to S is flat because it factors through the open subscheme Spec(A) of S and B_g/IB_g is flat over A. By [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], Z\cap U is a relative effective Cartier divisor on U over S.
